description: Between 1907 and 1920, **Picasso** and **Braque** broke the object into facets seen from several angles at once. The most radical revolution since the Renaissance.

hero.hook: What if a painting was no longer a window, but an object reconstructed from all angles?

blocks.text: Cubism was born between **1907** and **1908**. It is perhaps the most radical revolution since the perspective of the [[Quattrocento]], the Italian 15th century. **Pablo Picasso** and **George Braque** break the object into geometric fragments.
No more window painting on the world. The painter no longer copies nature: he reconstructs it. This deconstruction opens the way to abstract art.

Before Cubism, **Paul Cézanne** sought the solidity of forms behind changing light. He advises “treating nature through the cylinder, the sphere, the cone”. In his views of Sainte-Victoire mountain, he flattens the space and multiplies the points of view thanks to the [[passages]], these areas where the planes merge.

blocks.caption: Cézanne: nature seen as an assembly of volumes.

blocks.text: In 1907, Picasso described his visit to the Trocadéro museum not as a lesson in beauty, but as an exorcism in the face of the power of masks.

In **1907**, Picasso discovered the [[Trocadéro]] at the [[African and Oceanian arts]] ethnography museum. Masks do not copy the face: they conceptualize it. The object is no longer painted as we see it, but as we know it.

sections.title: Cézanne and the clash of masks

blocks.text: In **1907**, Picasso completed *The Young Ladies of Avignon*. Five nudes with sharp facets; some faces become masks. Even , his poet friend, is stunned. [[Apollinaire]]

blocks.caption: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon: the point of no return.

blocks.text: From **1908** to **1912**, Picasso and Braque invented **analytical cubism**. They observe a volume from all angles and pose these views at the same time on the canvas. The color almost disappears: gray and ochre, to force the eye into space. Small clues (a key, a guitar string) prevent us from falling into total abstraction.
They pushed the collaboration so far that they sometimes dressed as workers, to emphasize the artisanal side of their research.

Around **1912**, faced with the risk of illegibility, they invented **synthetic cubism**. We no longer cut the object into a thousand fragments: we summarize it by its clearest signs. Then the [[collage]] appears: newspapers, wallpaper stuck on the canvas.

blocks.caption: The collage: reality enters the painting.

blocks.text: Braque, a former painter-decorator, painted fake wood with a steel comb so perfect that they seemed more real than the actually glued wood.
The color returns. The shapes widen. A guitar can just be a curve. The painting is no longer a mirror: it is an autonomous object, constructed according to its own laws.

Cubism spread quickly. **Juan Gray** brings mathematical rigor to it; the [[Puteaux Group]] adapts it to the aesthetics of the machine. The movement nourishes Italian futurism, the abstraction of Mondrian, and influences as well as architecture. [[graphic design]]

blocks.text: Above all, the viewer becomes active: it is up to him to recompose the image. Art finally separates itself from simple imitation.
By breaking the Renaissance perspective and inventing collage, Picasso and Braque transformed the painting into mental architecture, more of a mirror of reality.

sections.title: A legacy that goes beyond painting
